summary.headline: RVNL standalone Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin fell to 5.83% from 10.36% in Q3 on onerous contracts, despite revenue up 47.6% QoQ.
summary.overview: Standalone Q4 FY26 turnover rose 47.6% QoQ and 4.78% YoY (as stated, with a separate 0.72% YoY figure cited), but standalone EBITDA fell 26.74% YoY and PAT fell 32% YoY. Management attributed the margin squeeze to a few onerous contracts and JV reconciliation adjustments, citing an INR 54 crore onerous-contract charge and INR 35 crore SPV reconciliation. Total order book stood at INR 99,262 crore at March 31, 2026, with standalone FY26 inflows of INR 5,875 crore. Management guided to 15-20% revenue growth and better margins in FY27, while acknowledging Q1 FY27 would be slightly challenging.

segments.name: Building works
segments.commentary: Management said building works contributed 31.40% of revenue from operations, up 129.50% YoY.

segments.name: Order book mix
segments.commentary: Railways INR 57,000 crore, signalling INR 14,900 crore, ports/roads/highways INR 10,400 crore, metros INR 9,900 crore, power and transmission about INR 4,000 crore, hydro and irrigation INR 2,000 crore.

segments.name: Bidding execution
segments.commentary: Execution from bidding works rose to INR 6,283 crore in FY26 from INR 2,737 crore in FY25 (about 129% increase).

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at around 15-20%, with margins expected to be much better than FY26.
Management expects margin improvement from Q1 FY27 after the onerous-contract adjustment, though Q1 FY27 described as slightly challenging.
BharatNet (INR 13,236 crore, 8,206 km OFC, 15.01% physical progress) expected to deliver good revenue and margins this year.
Rishikesh Karnaprayag rail project (INR 37,000 crore, 125 km, 74% overall progress, about 96% tunnel excavation) targeted for completion by December 2029.
Vande Bharat sleeper (INR 14,400 crore, 35-year maintenance) first prototype targeted December 2026; five sets in first supply year, 120 sets over five years.
capex_capacity: Vande Bharat sleeper rakes executed by SPV Kinet Railway Solutions; two prototypes to be built this year, with trials taking three to four months after prototype supply.
Management cited digital execution tools: progress tracking versus plan, drone site inspections and dashboards across supervisory and top management levels.
Bidding strategy targets at least 5-10% profit on each bidding work rather than aggressive bidding.
demand_pricing: Order book split roughly 50:50 between nomination and competitive bidding; about INR 45,000 crore each per management, with about 30,000 crore of railway works in pipeline on nomination basis.
Pursuing PMC (project management consultancy) work from PSUs and government; recent wins include NMDC and Visakhapatnam Port Trust.
One JV bidding work of INR 400 crore won recently from railways; JV inflows for Q4 and FY26 not separately quantified beyond this.
Price variation clauses in most contracts mitigate commodity inflation, though management acknowledged challenges remain; some contracts are fixed-price.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins recover from Q1 FY27, or is the ~4-4.5% EBITDA margin the new base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 PAT was hit by an INR 54 crore onerous contract and INR 35 crore SPV reconciliation and municipal tax on new building; adjusted PAT was slightly better than Q3, and margins expected to improve from Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables rise and cash fall in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR 3,400 crore was recoverable from Ministry of Railways and was not collected within FY26; it was received in April 2026, which drove negative cash flow.

qa_highlights.question: Recovery outlook on Krishnapatnam Railway Company receivables of INR 1,116 crore (including INR 890 crore interest)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about INR 290 crore was recovered last year and KRCL paid a INR 50 crore dividend, of which RVNL received INR 25 crore; receivables expected to be largely cleared within about two years.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 top-line and margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided revenue growth of around 15-20% and margins much better than FY26, with Q1 FY27 slightly challenging.

qa_highlights.question: Order book split between nomination and competitive bidding, and order inflow including JVs?
qa_highlights.answer: Split is roughly 50:50; management said bidding is not being pursued aggressively, targeting 5-10% profit per bid. JV inflow was one INR 400 crore railway bid.

qa_highlights.question: Vande Bharat delivery timeline after prototype?
qa_highlights.answer: Two prototypes planned in 2026; first-year supply of five sets after trials of three to four months, rising to 120 sets over five years.

qa_highlights.question: Steps for faster execution and defence logistics opportunities?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited digital tools (progress tracking, drones, dashboards); on defence logistics it said work is underway but would not be detailed on the call.

risks_watch: Standalone EBITDA margin at 5.83% in Q4 FY26 versus 10.36% in Q3; whether margins recover in Q1 FY27 as guided.
Receivables from Ministry of Railways (INR 3,400 crore received only in April 2026) and KRCL receivables of INR 1,116 crore including INR 890 crore interest.
Further onerous contract charges and JV reconciliation adjustments.
Commodity cost inflation on competitive bids and execution delays on BharatNet and Rishikesh Karnaprayag projects.
Vande Bharat prototype delivery timing (December 2026 target).
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY27 growth and margin recovery, but cautious on Q4 profitability and Q1 FY27, which management said would be slightly challenging. Responses on cash flow and receivables were direct; the defence-logistics question was deflected as not for discussion on the call.
key_quotes: Although this year has been challenging for the company, RVNL has remained focused on sustaining its operational performance and ensuring timely execution of key projects.
And even the margins will definitely increase. That I want to assure you. And it will be much better than this year.
Cash flow is a challenge, because we are working for Ministry of Railways, and we have to get money from Ministry of Railways.
